title: Roasted Cauliflower with Tahini Dressing
subtitle: Caramelised cauliflower florets with a lemony tahini sauce and fresh herbs
excerpt: Cauliflower florets roasted until golden and nutty, served warm on a lemony tahini sauce with chopped parsley, pomegranate seeds and a scattering of toasted pine nuts. A Middle Eastern-influenced salad with real depth.
sourceNotes: Roasted cauliflower with tahini reflects the influence of Levantine and Israeli cooking on contemporary British and American food culture, an influence accelerated by the work of Yotam Ottolenghi from the mid-2000s onward. Tahini (sesame paste) has been central to Eastern Mediterranean cooking for centuries; its pairing with roasted vegetables, particularly cauliflower, became widely known in British home cooking through cookbooks and restaurant menus from around 2010.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Roast the cauliflower and make the tahini sauce up to 2 hours ahead. Assemble just before serving.

content.text: Roasted cauliflower with tahini earns its place from the combination of caramelised, nutty cauliflower and the sesame richness of the tahini sauce. The cauliflower must be properly roasted: deeply golden in places, with some crisp edges. Pale, steam-cooked florets have nothing to offer. The tahini sauce loosened with lemon juice and water goes sharp and silky and pulls the whole plate together.

Heat the oven to 220 C. Toss the cauliflower florets with {{olive-oil}} of olive oil, {{cumin-ground}} of ground cumin and 0.75 tsp of salt. Spread in a single layer on a baking tray. Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, turning once, until the florets are deeply golden and caramelised at the edges.

Stir together {{tahini}} of tahini, the juice of {{lemon}} lemon, {{garlic}} of crushed garlic and 0.25 tsp of salt. The mixture will seize and thicken. Add cold water a tablespoon at a time, stirring until the sauce reaches a pourable consistency, like double cream.

Spread the tahini sauce across a large plate or shallow bowl. Pile the warm roasted cauliflower on top. Scatter over the parsley, {{pine-nuts}} of toasted pine nuts and pomegranate seeds if using. Serve immediately.

items.symptom: Tahini sauce is too thick and stiff
items.cause: Tahini seizes with lemon juice before the water is added.
items.fix: Add cold water one tablespoon at a time, stirring vigorously. The sauce will suddenly loosen as the emulsion forms. Aim for the consistency of pourable yoghurt.

items.cause: Florets too large, tray overcrowded, or oven not hot enough.
items.fix: Use a very hot oven (220 C). Cut the florets small. Give them space on the tray so heat can circulate.

content.text: Roasted cauliflower with tahini is part of the wider shift in British cooking toward Middle Eastern flavours that took hold in the 2000s. Cauliflower turns out to be one of the vegetables that roasts best: it caramelises well and handles bold flavours. This is one of the dishes that changed how British cooks thought about the vegetable.
